context: Built against spec revision 3 (PaymentProvider and Outcome, PayPal Sandbox wire mapping, 005_fake_paypal.sql semantics, fake approval listener SEC-12 and F-TR-14, SEC-3 approval host, SEC-5 webhook key) and e0's handoff ho-mv37ojw0-01fb7411 (stub, signer, contract suite and its factory contract). LIVE-DEPENDENT: sandbox.js is verified only against test/helpers/paypal-stub.js and injected fetch functions; no Sandbox host was contacted, no credential exists, RS_LIVE_MODEL and RS_LIVE_PAYPAL were never set; issue names, link rels and status sets stay the spec's guesses until test:live-paypal runs (OQ-D5 open). The one verified lesson shown at claim does not apply (see lessonDecisions).

completedWork: (1) src/payments/provider.js: the port (PROVIDER_METHODS, CALL_KINDS, Outcome constructors ok/rejected/retryable/unknown, toPayPalValue, checkArguments, webhookInput, assertPaymentProvider) and createPayments({config, db, clock, log, appOrigin}) -> {provider, listener, close} which imports the adapter named by config.paymentProvider. A bad argument is a rejected 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT before anything is sent or stored. (2) fake.js: createFakeProvider({db, clock, log, testHooks, webhookSecret, approvalOrigin, pid, freeze}); each call is ONE BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction (fault take, replay or effect, fake_paypal_calls row), so processes agree and counts are exact; merchant-scoped lookups; faults read from fault_flags (scenario faults, lost_response/timeout/http_<4xx|5xx>/bad_body per call kind incl. reads and verify_webhook, hooks only with testHooks); approveFakeOrder, loadFakeOrder, takeFakePaypalFault, parseFakeFault, fakeWebhookSignature exported; verifyWebhook is the HMAC scheme of webhook-signer.js; the default freeze sends SIGSTOP to the process (checked in a scratch two-process run: stopped after the capture commit, result returned after SIGCONT). (5) merchants.js: SUPPLIER_MERCHANT_KEYS, merchantMode, activeMerchantKeys, isActiveMerchantKey, merchantKeyForSupplier, merchantCredentials (Secret values), sandboxMerchants, describeMerchants (secret-free). (6) src/config.js: RS_EXPLAIN_REPHRASE parsing and config.explainRephrase removed (FU-25); RS_MODEL_TIMEOUT_MS bounded to 1..40000 (MAX_MODEL_TIMEOUT_MS), default 30000 (FU-27). (7) Tests: fake.test.js 41, sandbox.test.js 35, merchants.test.js 14 (incl. 'TR-D-7: RS_MODEL_TIMEOUT_MS above 40000 is refused ...' and the FU-25 test, placed here because test/unit/config/limits.test.js is outside e1's ownership), provider-contract.test.js runs e0's suite twice (216 tests: 209 pass, 7 skipped), fake-approval-headers.test.js 18. Defects found by the tests and fixed before completion: the fake's verifyWebhook opened a nested transaction when it had to create the SEC-5 key (contract suite); the Sandbox adapter returned bad_body for an authorization the double reports already EXPIRED (contract suite, auth_expire); the fake counted a verifyWebhook call with an unusable body (fake.test.js); TextDecoder stripped a leading BOM from a webhook body, so the spliced bytes were not the received ones (sandbox.test.js). A mutation (a second CSP header appended in the listener) was caught by 5 header tests and reverted. Verification command: 484 tests, 477 pass, 0 fail, 7 skipped (the 7 are the fake harness's OAuth and wire scenarios, skipped because supports() is false or wire is null, not passed). npm test: 1800 tests, 1781 pass, 4 fail, 15 skipped; the 4 failures are the direct consequence of FU-25 in files outside e1's ownership (see remainingIssues 1); the 15 skips are the 7 above plus the 8 contract scenarios waiting for phase E routes.
remainingIssues: FU-25 BREAKS 4 TESTS OUTSIDE E1'S OWNERSHIP (npm test: ev:ev-mv38e6wu-01748302 and ev:ev-mv38bsgw-01e94ad3, 4 fail): test/unit/config/defaults.test.js asserts c.explainRephrase false (line 38) and true with RS_EXPLAIN_REPHRASE=1 (lines 84 and 124); test/unit/config/limits.test.js 'boolean switches accept only 0 or 1' lists RS_EXPLAIN_REPHRASE (line 76); test/scan/env-example.test.js has RS_EXPLAIN_REPHRASE in its DEFAULTS table (line 65) and .env.example still lists it (line 93, g2 per the decision). Whoever owns those files (g2 or the orchestrator) must drop those lines; the replacement assertions already exist in test/unit/payments/merchants.test.js ('FU-25: ...'). Until then npm test is red by exactly these 4. Comments in src/ai/provider.js:11 and src/ai/rephrase.js:1 still mention the variable (not e1 files).

FOR E2 (construction): after app.listen(), call createPayments({config, db, clock, log, appOrigin: () => app.deps.publicUrl()}) and assign app.deps.payments = payments.provider (ctx is spread from deps per request, so late assignment works); close() on shutdown. Pass voidProvider to createApp separately: its queueVoid(db, intent) must INSERT OR IGNORE so:<supplierOrderId>:void:1 into provider_calls (c3 port, FU-19). The listener is started inside createPayments only for the fake and is null for the Sandbox; its origin is what createOrder returns as approvalUrl (default port 0, so tests read listener.port). merchantKeyForSupplier(config, supplierCode) gives the merchantKey for every provider call (fake: the supplier code; Sandbox: per merchant mode); isActiveMerchantKey(config, key) is the webhook route's 'configured key else 404' check. The return handler's crash hook is takeFakePaypalFault(db, 'crash_after_return_commit', {merchantKey, testHooks: config.testHooks}).

FOR E2/E3/E4 (Outcomes): ok values are the port shapes plus provider and simulated (fake) or provider and sandbox (Sandbox). authorizeOrder status is CREATED, PENDING or DENIED (an authorization already EXPIRED when PayPal answers is reported CREATED with its past expirationTime). Definitive rejections to expect: INVALID_ARGUMENT (400, nothing sent), MERCHANT_NOT_CONFIGURED, APPROVAL_HOST_INVALID and APPROVAL_LINK_MISSING (createOrder: the order exists at PayPal but is unusable), WEBHOOK_ID_MISSING (verifyWebhook without a webhook id; the route decides its answer), REQUEST_ID_KIND_MISMATCH, ORDER_NOT_APPROVED, ORDER_ALREADY_AUTHORIZED, AUTHORIZATION_ALREADY_CAPTURED / _VOIDED / _EXPIRED / _PENDING / _DENIED / _AMOUNT_EXCEEDED, AUTHORIZATION_CANNOT_BE_VOIDED, CAPTURE_FULLY_REFUNDED, CAPTURE_NOT_COMPLETED, REFUND_AMOUNT_EXCEEDED. The fake alone also answers retryable 429 FAKE_DB_BUSY. verifyWebhook returns ok {verified:false} (never an error) for missing or malformed signature headers or a body that is not one JSON object.

FOR E3/E4/E6 (fake behaviour): a fake PENDING authorization, capture or refund never settles by itself; tests move it with SQL on fake_paypal_* (there is no settle helper). verify_webhook calls are counted in fake_paypal_calls (kind 'verify_webhook'), approval-page requests are not. fake_paypal_calls.resource_id is the id of the resource a call created, else the one it addressed. Faults are consumed inside the call's own transaction; a fault row whose value is a supplier code applies only to that merchant key. The test-only faults are ignored (and stay armed) unless createFakeProvider got testHooks: true (createPayments passes config.testHooks). Fault kinds beyond the admin list work too (every call kind, http_<400-599>, bad_body) for tests that insert fault_flags rows directly. freeze_* default to process.kill(pid, 'SIGSTOP') (POSIX only); a unit test can inject freeze.

SPEC GAPS RESOLVED (to confirm in review): (a) order status of the fake after authorize is COMPLETED and after a void VOIDED; (b) the fake stores only ok answers in fake_paypal_requests, like the stub; (c) a void is allowed on CREATED and PENDING authorizations; (d) fake auth_expire stores expiration_time = now and reads show EXPIRED (persisted lazily as status EXPIRED); (e) the fake approval page lists a merchant label 'Merchant <key> (simulated)' and has no stylesheet because style-src 'self' with exactly three routes leaves nowhere to serve one; (f) the listener adds Cache-Control: no-store to the app's headers; (g) argument validation limits: ids [A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}, request id [A-Za-z0-9._:-]{1,108}, amountCents 1..999999999, USD only, return/cancel URLs http(s) without credentials up to 2048 chars, webhook body 1..65536 bytes; (h) whitespace OUTSIDE the webhook JSON object is not covered by the Sandbox path, because the double (and PayPal's parser) verify the member span, which excludes it, while the fake signs every byte.

LIMITS: the Sandbox adapter proves agreement with the simulation and the spec's Outcome classes only; the real issue names, link rels (payer-action vs approve), status sets, the 29-day expiry, token lifetime and the verify-webhook request shape are unconfirmed until test:live-paypal runs. The timeout cases use real 400-500 ms AbortSignal bounds (about 5 s in the contract suite). The approval listener's behaviour in a real browser (form-action across the 303 chain) is not re-tested here; fake-approval-headers.test.js pins the bytes, the earlier Playwright run is ev:ev-mv1dsh6c-019c5a8d.
Process note: the tests were written after the code; each defect listed in completedWork was found by a test and fixed before completion, not by a failing test written first.

lessonDecisions.note: The lesson applies when designing a hook or guard that maps file writes to a project record or root in a repository with several records; this task designs no hook, guard or root discovery, so its 'Applies when' list does not hold. The guard accepted every nested write here and correctly refused an inline python file writer, asking for the Edit tool.
